characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Specimens electrolytically polished and etched (1 g ferric chloride + 10 ml hydrochloric acid + 10 ml deionized water); longitudinal section (RD×ND); 100 µm scale bar in Fig. 3(e).
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 90% reduction grains are visibly elongated along RD and the matrix is almost entirely consumed by dark shear bands; the second deformation stage (70–90%) is characterized by the gradual development of shear bands.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the morphology and evolution of the cold rolling microstructure (shear bands, grain elongation).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2100 transmission electron microscope; twin-jet electro-polished specimens (30% nitric acid + 70% methyl alcohol); 1 µm scale bar in Fig. 6(c).
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 6(c) shows dark, dense, elongated dislocation-tangle and cell walls in a lighter matrix; dislocation cell structure indicates that dislocation cross slip is operated at the highest reduction; the dislocation tangle structure has an average size of 0.49 μm.
characterization_methods.purpose: Detail the deformation substructure (dislocation tangles/cells) of the 90% cold rolled sample.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/MAX 2500PC x-ray diffractometer; measured on the RD×TD plane; ODFs and Fmax calculated by the Arbitrarily Defined Cells method; φ2 = 0°, 45°, 65° ODF sections (Fig. 8) and fiber intensity plots (Fig. 9).
characterization_methods.key_findings: Weak overall texture; α-fiber texture monotonously increased up to 90% reduction; weak γ-fiber orientations at 90% (relatively significant at {111}〈110〉 E position); the β-fiber Goss component monotonously increased with a continuous B→Goss shift; the 90% ODF sections contain level 8–9 cores; transition from copper-type to brass-type texture occurs at 50% reduction.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the rolling texture evolution of the 90% cold rolled sample.
characterization_methods.technique: X-ray diffraction (XRD) texture measurement (pole figures, ODF)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SHIMADZU AG-X50KN universal testing machine; dog-bone specimen (gauge length 16 mm, width 4 mm) cut along the rolling direction.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 90% rolled sample: yield strength of ~2.0 GPa (≈3.5 times the as-quenched state) with greatly reduced uniform elongation and loss of work-hardening capability; engineering/true stress-strain curves shown in Fig. 1.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; three parallel tests per condition
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate the tensile mechanical properties of the 90% cold rolled material.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates the critical shear stress for twinning to the stacking fault energy and the partial dislocation Burgers vector.
analytical_models.model_name: Critical shear stress for deformation twinning (τ_c)
analytical_models.model_note: Resulting critical stress calculated as ~1.48 GPa.

computational_details.simulation_method: analytical calculation of the critical shear stress for deformation twinning
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated critical stress (~1.48 GPa) is much higher than the maximum resolved shear stress (~0.75 GPa), yet twinning indeed occurs during cold rolling; this is explained by SRO-dislocation interaction lowering the actual critical shear stress and by local stress concentration from inhomogeneous strain.

analytical_models.equation_role: Strengthening due to long-range interaction between coplanar slip bands; depends on the average slip band distance D.
analytical_models.model_note: Later microbands, twins, shear bands and dislocation tangles enhance strength through Hall-Petch effects; the ultrahigh yield strength of ~2.0 GPa is eventually realized.

computational_details.simulation_method: analytical strengthening model for the Taylor lattice

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation cross slip / cell wall formation
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dislocation cell/tangle structure with average size 0.49 μm develops at the highest reduction; dislocation cross slip activated at higher rolling degrees.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: microshear band formation by local strain concentration
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Shear bands consist of ultrafine grains (confirmed by continuous diffraction rings) and progressively consume the matrix; shear bands and twins scatter the texture.

interfaces.interface_notes: The weak overall texture of the 90% rolled steel is attributed to the dislocation planar glide (planar slip causing unusual crystal lattice rotation), while inhomogeneous deformation substructures such as microbands, shear bands and twins also scatter the texture.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocation planar glide dominates the rolling deformation (striking feature of the steel); cross slip is activated at higher rolling degrees (observable at 90% via the dislocation cell structure).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Yield strength: ~2.0 GPa after 90% cold rolling versus ~570 MPa in the as-quenched state (~3.5 times increase); simultaneously the material loses work-hardening capability and the uniform elongation decreases (strength-ductility trade-off).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-forged into bars 60 mm in diameter; finish forging temperature 900 °C.
Cold rolled to 90% thickness reduction (ε = 2.3); this is the maximum cold rolling reduction studied. Sheet dimensions 40 mm width, 70 mm length before rolling.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens cut along the rolling direction; SHIMADZU AG-X50KN universal testing machine; three parallel tests per condition.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone shaped, gauge length 16 mm, width 4 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 1(a) engineering stress–strain and Fig. 1(b) true stress–strain curves; the 90% curve rises steeply to the top of the axis at very low strain and fractures early, showing loss of work-hardening capability.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: grains visibly elongated along the rolling direction (RD)

phases_present.morphology: grains strongly elongated along RD; matrix almost entirely consumed by dark shear bands
dark, dense, elongated dislocation-tangle and cell walls in a lighter matrix

grain_structure.texture: Weak overall rolling texture; α-fiber strengthened up to 90% reduction; weak γ-fiber orientation at 90% (E {111}〈110〉); brass-type texture developed at higher reductions; maximum-intensity β-fiber position shifts from B toward Goss.

phases_present.texture: Rolling texture is weak. At 90% reduction the α-fiber texture monotonously increased up to 90% rolling reduction; weak orientations near γ-fiber appear at 90% reduction (slightly strengthened, relatively significant at the {111}〈110〉 E position). The α-fiber Brass {110}〈112〉 component increased and scattered to Goss, with the maximum intensity position shifting from φ1 = 45° to 20° at reductions >50%. A weak {552}〈115〉 CuT component detected at 70% spreads to lower Φ after 90%. The β-fiber Goss orientation monotonously increased, with a continuous shift from B towards Goss; along the β-fiber the 90% curve rises above f(g) = 7.0 near φ2 ≈ 85–90°, and the 90% ODF sections contain level 8–9 cores. Overall the texture transitions from 'copper-type' to 'brass-type' at 50% rolling reduction.

structures.overall_structure: After 90% cold rolling the microstructure is dominated by abundant shear bands; grains are visibly elongated along the rolling direction (RD) and the matrix is almost entirely consumed by dark shear bands. At the highest strain, dislocation tangles and a dislocation cell structure also develop. The deformation substructure evolution during cold rolling approximately follows the sequence: Taylor lattice → microbands → twins → shear bands → dislocation tangles.

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C steel was estimated as ~108 mJ/m² and the Burgers vector of a partial dislocation as 0.146 nm.

The maximum resolved shear stress during cold rolling was ~0.75 GPa, well below the calculated twinning critical stress (~1.48 GPa); twinning nonetheless occurred, attributed to short-range order (SRO) in the austenitic matrix and local stress concentration.

For the 90% rolled sample, Fig. 1(a)/1(b) show the engineering and true stress-strain curves reaching near the 2100 MPa axis limit at very low strain before early fracture (individual numeric stress/strain values are not tabulated for the 90% condition).

Fig. 6(c) is captioned as the bright-field image of dislocation tangles of 90% cold rolling reduction; the manuscript sentence associating the 0.49 μm dislocation tangle structure with this figure sits within the 70% reduction paragraph, creating minor ambiguity in attribution.
